messages:
mike_r: Heads up — saw a batch of OOMs on prod-gpu-pool-3 during a long-context pass ( > 30k tokens ). KV cache kept growing instead of stabilizing. Dumped profiles and KV stats, attaching below. Anyone seen this growth pattern before?

aya: Oof. Which model/quant/kernel? rough timestamps?

mike_r: Model: rwd-large-v1 (int8 quant), kernel switch to `fast_matmul_v2` around 16k seq during inference. Spike starts ~2026-03-17T09:12Z. KV bytes climbs steadily until OOM at ~0.95 * GPU_RAM.

jamie: I grabbed a perf profile and a flamegraph. Link: https://perf.internal/runs/2367890123/flame (internal)

jamie: Profiling snippet:
```
kv_allocs: 1.8GB -> 7.6GB over 10k tokens
kv_fragmentation_est: 28%
kernel_switch_counts: { default: 1, fast_matmul_v2: 3 }
batch_size_peak: 96 (burst)
```

linda: That fragmentation number is worrying. Could be slab fragmentation + small-slab churn from batching bursts. Did we try aggressive compaction?

jamie: We disabled background compaction in that build to avoid CPU interference. Turns out `fast_matmul_v2` pins some intermediate buffers to separate alloc arenas, which prevents reuse by the KV slab allocator. So overall usable memory drops even though nominal free pages exist.

aya: So two contributing factors: (1) kernel selection causing pinned arenas; (2) batching bursts creating many short-lived KV entries -> fragmentation and small free holes.

mike_r: TL;DR: KV bytes growth is real (not leak) but reuse is blocked. We should mitigate short-term and plan longer-term allocator changes.

jamie: Short-term mitigations I've put in a draft patch:
- re-enable background compaction with low cpu cap
- soft-evict older KV prefixes when slab_util > 0.78
- throttle batching bursts for long-context sessions (`burst_limit=32`)

Config snippet:
```
kv.compaction.enabled = true
kv.compaction.cpu_pct = 5
kv.soft_evict_threshold = 0.78
inference.batching.burst_limit = 32
```

linda: Love the soft-evict idea. We should be careful with correctness (evicting prefixes affects cache hits). Propose evicting only full-history prefixes older than last turn and keep last N tokens pinned for immediate response.

aya: Another safe fallback: if slab_util > 0.9 for > 2s, gracefully degrade to shorter context mode by truncating prefix or route to a smaller model variant. That avoids hard OOMs.

jamie: Agreed. Proposed runtime guard pseudocode:
```
if slab_util > 0.9 and persist(2s):
  route(request, model_variant="rwd-medium")
  emit(metric="kv.fallback.model_swap")
```

mike_r: Can we canary these changes in prod-gpu-pool-3 canary group? I want to limit blast radius.

infra-bot: deploybot: started canary rollout for `kv-soft-evict-v1` to prod-gpu-pool-3-canary (10% hosts). (deploy id: dpl-8932) :rocket:

srebot: incident created: INC-2026-0317-01 — OOM surge on prod-gpu-pool-3. @oncall please monitor.

jamie: Experiment plan:
- metric set: slab_util, kv_frag_est, kv_alloc_bytes, p50/p95 latency, 503_rate
- compare baseline 24h -> canary 24h
- acceptance: p95 latency delta < 5%, 503_rate <= baseline + 0.1% and no OOMs for 24h.

aya: I'll own the dashboard and alerts. mike_r please own rollout and rollback criteria. jamie will own patch and unit tests. linda will review compaction correctness.

mike_r: Sounds good. I'll pause pushing other runtime kernel changes while canary is live. If we still see OOMs we fallback to routing to dedicated batch nodes with disk-backed spill.

linda: One more note for longer-term — we should look at allocator redesign: coalescing adjacent free slots across arenas or a small-ring global freelist to avoid cross-arena starvation when kernels pin. Filing a follow-up RFC.

jamie: Filed RFC: https://rfc.internal/kv-allocator-ring (draft).

mike_r: Thanks all. Action items: jamie PR + tests, canary rollout (infra), dashboard (aya), review compaction correctness (linda). Will update thread with canary metrics. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout complete to 10% hosts (dpl-8932). Monitoring for 30m.

srebot: alert: slab_util exceeded 0.88 on one canary host, auto-soft-evict triggered, no OOM. Logged event id evt-2367890450.

mike_r: Nice — soft-evict worked on the canary. Let's keep monitoring and prepare to widen to 50% if stable for 6h.

aya: Noted. I'll post baseline vs canary graphs in 2h.
